title: Psalms Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 20.

questions.question: In Psalms 20:1, who is asked to hear in the day of trouble?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:1 says, 'The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble,' indicating that the LORD is asked to hear in the day of trouble.

questions.question: According to Psalms 20:1, whose name is asked to defend thee?
questions.correctAnswer: The God of Jacob
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:1 states, 'the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;' indicating the God of Jacob is invoked for defense.

questions.question: From where does Psalms 20:2 say help is sent?
questions.correctAnswer: From the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:2 says, 'Send thee help from the sanctuary,' which is the source of help.

questions.question: What does Psalms 20:2 say will be given out of Zion?
questions.correctAnswer: Strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:2 states, 'and strengthen thee out of Zion;' indicating strength is given from Zion.

questions.question: What does Psalms 20:3 ask the LORD to remember?
questions.correctAnswer: Thy offerings
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:3 says, 'Remember all thy offerings,' indicating that the offerings should be remembered.

questions.question: In Psalms 20:3, what else is asked to be accepted besides offerings?
questions.correctAnswer: Thy burnt sacrifice
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:3 states, 'and accept thy burnt sacrifice;' along with offerings, burnt sacrifices are to be accepted.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:1 is a Psalm of Solomon.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:1 identifies the Psalm as 'A Psalm of David,' not Solomon.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:2 mentions help coming from Zion.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:2 says, 'and strengthen thee out of Zion;' confirming help and strength come from Zion.

questions.question: According to Psalms 20:4, what is granted according to thine own heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Counsel
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:4 says, 'Grant thee according to thine own heart, and fulfil all thy counsel,' implying counsel is granted.

questions.question: Who does Psalms 20:6 say the LORD saveth?
questions.correctAnswer: His anointed
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:6 states, 'Now know I that the LORD saveth his anointed;'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:7 says some trust in chariots and horses.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:7 reads, 'Some trust in chariots, and some in horses,' confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: According to Psalms 20:8, what is the condition of those who trust in chariots and horses?
options: They are brought down and fallen
questions.correctAnswer: They are brought down and fallen
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:8 states, 'They are brought down and fallen;' referring to those who trust in chariots and horses.

questions.question: In Psalms 20:5, what do 'we' set up in the name of our God?
questions.correctAnswer: Our banners
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:5 says, 'in the name of our God we will set up our banners,' showing what is set up.

questions.question: Which of these instructions comes first in Psalms 20?
options: Send thee help from the sanctuary
The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble
Grant thee according to thine own heart
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble
questions.explanation: The first instruction is in Psalms 20:1, 'The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble;' followed by sending help and remembering offerings.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:9 is a prayer for the king to be saved and to hear when we call.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:9 says, 'Save, LORD: let the king hear us when we call,' confirming it is a prayer for the king.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 20:4, what does God grant and fulfill for the believer?
options: According to thine own heart and all thy counsel
Only what is easy and pleasing
questions.correctAnswer: According to thine own heart and all thy counsel
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:4 states that God grants according to the believer's own heart and fulfills all counsel, emphasizing personal alignment with God's will.

questions.question: How does Psalms 20:5 describe the response of the people to God's salvation?
options: They rejoice and set up banners in the name of God
They seek revenge on their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoice and set up banners in the name of God
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes rejoicing in salvation and raising banners in God's name, symbolizing public celebration and trust in God's protection (Psalms 20:5).

questions.question: What assurance does Psalms 20:6 give about God's relationship with His anointed?
options: The LORD saveth his anointed and hears him from heaven
The LORD ignores the anointed in times of trouble
The LORD only helps those who are wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD saveth his anointed and hears him from heaven
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:6 assures that God saves His anointed and hears their prayers with the power of His right hand, emphasizing divine protection and intervention.

questions.question: What does Psalms 20:4-5 together teach about the connection between a believer's desires and God’s response?
options: God grants desires aligned with the believer’s heart and causes rejoicing in salvation
God ignores the believer’s desires but rewards good deeds
Believers must earn favor through sacrifices alone
Desires are irrelevant; only fasting matters
questions.correctAnswer: God grants desires aligned with the believer’s heart and causes rejoicing in salvation
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 show that when desires align with God’s counsel, He grants them, leading to rejoicing in salvation and public declaration of faith.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 20:6, how can believers have confidence in prayer during difficult times?
options: Because the LORD saves His anointed and hears from heaven with saving strength
Because God only listens to the perfect
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD saves His anointed and hears from heaven with saving strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:6 teaches that God’s saving power and attentive hearing of His anointed provide confidence and assurance in prayer amidst trials.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith does Psalms 20:7 teach by contrasting trust in chariots and horses with trust in God's name?
options: True faith trusts in God rather than worldly strength or weapons
Faith requires military power to be effective
Trusting in God means avoiding all action
Horses and chariots are better than prayer
questions.correctAnswer: True faith trusts in God rather than worldly strength or weapons
questions.explanation: Verse 7 contrasts reliance on military might with reliance on God's name, teaching believers to place their faith in divine power over worldly means.

questions.question: What promise does Psalms 20:8 give to those who trust in the LORD rather than in horses and chariots?
options: They are risen and stand upright while others fall
They will be defeated and brought down
questions.correctAnswer: They are risen and stand upright while others fall
questions.explanation: Verse 8 promises that those trusting in the LORD will rise and stand firm, whereas those relying on horses and chariots fall, illustrating spiritual victory.

questions.question: How does Psalms 20:5 show the importance of community in celebrating God’s salvation?
options: The verse says 'We will rejoice' and set up banners, indicating collective praise
It describes only the king celebrating alone
It emphasizes silent, private worship only
questions.correctAnswer: The verse says 'We will rejoice' and set up banners, indicating collective praise
questions.explanation: The plural 'we' in Psalms 20:5 highlights communal rejoicing and public expression of faith, emphasizing fellowship in worship and trust.

questions.question: What connection can be drawn between offering sacrifices and receiving help from God as seen in Psalms 20:2-3?
options: God strengthens and helps those who remember and offer sacrifices
Sacrifices are irrelevant to God's help
God only helps those who never make sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: God strengthens and helps those who remember and offer sacrifices
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 link God's strengthening help from Zion with remembering and offering sacrifices, showing obedience and worship invite divine assistance.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:1 teaches that God defends His people specifically in the day of trouble.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:1 explicitly states the LORD hears in the day of trouble and defends in the name of the God of Jacob, confirming divine protection in hardship.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 20:9, the psalmist asks that the king be saved and hear the people’s call.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 9 is a prayer asking the LORD to save and let the king hear when the people call, showing intercession for leadership.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:6 suggests that God's help is limited and uncertain for His anointed.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Contrary to the statement, Psalms 20:6 affirms God's sure salvation and attentive hearing for His anointed, showing certainty in divine help.

questions.question: If a believer aligns their desires with God’s counsel as in Psalms 20:4, what outcome is promised in the next verse (Psalms 20:5)?
options: The LORD will fulfill all petitions and there will be rejoicing in salvation
The believer will face greater trials
The believer will be ignored by God
The believer must make more sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will fulfill all petitions and there will be rejoicing in salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:5 follows verse 4 by promising that God fulfills petitions and inspires communal rejoicing, linking obedience with joyful blessing.

questions.question: A fellow believer is discouraged because they rely on their own strength rather than God. Based on Psalms 20:7-8, what biblical truth can encourage them?
options: Trusting in the LORD leads to rising and standing upright, unlike trusting in chariots and horses
Self-reliance is the ultimate path to success
God favors those with the strongest armies
Trusting God means avoiding all effort
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in the LORD leads to rising and standing upright, unlike trusting in chariots and horses
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 teach that while some trust in military power and fall, those who trust in God will rise and stand firm, encouraging faith over self-reliance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 20:4-6 collectively teach about the relationship between prayer, God's will, and divine intervention?
options: God grants prayers aligned with His counsel, saves His anointed, and hears from heaven with power
Prayer guarantees any wish regardless of God's will
God only listens to sacrifices, not prayers
Divine intervention is random and not connected to prayer
questions.correctAnswer: God grants prayers aligned with His counsel, saves His anointed, and hears from heaven with power
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize that God responds to prayers that align with His will, saving and empowering the anointed from heaven, showing a dynamic prayer-divine action link.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 20.

questions.question: According to Psalms 20:7, in what do some people place their trust instead of the name of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Chariots and horses
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:7 explicitly states that some trust in chariots and horses, but the faithful remember the name of the LORD our God.

questions.question: What is the outcome for those who trust in chariots and horses compared to those who remember the name of the LORD, according to Psalms 20:8?
options: They fall, but we rise and stand upright
They remain strong, but we stumble
They are victorious, but we are defeated
questions.correctAnswer: They fall, but we rise and stand upright
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:8 contrasts the fate of the two groups by saying those who trust in chariots and horses are brought down and fallen, while those who trust in the LORD are risen and stand upright.

questions.question: What does the psalmist pray for in Psalms 20:9?
options: That the king will hear us when we call
questions.correctAnswer: That the king will hear us when we call
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:9 is a direct plea for the LORD to save and let the king hear when they call upon Him.

questions.question: The phrase 'the saving strength of his right hand' in Psalms 20:6 is a literary device known as:
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: The 'right hand' symbolizes power and authority, making it a metaphor for God's saving strength as described in Psalms 20:6.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also emphasizes trusting in God over military might, similar to Psalms 20:7-8?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 15:1-3
questions.explanation: Exodus 15:1-3 celebrates the LORD as a warrior who delivers His people, paralleling Psalms 20:7-8's theme of trusting God rather than weapons of war.

questions.question: In Psalms 20:4, what does the psalmist ask God to grant and fulfill?
options: According to thine own heart and all thy counsel
Peace and prosperity to the land
Strength and honor to the king
Mercy and forgiveness for the people
questions.correctAnswer: According to thine own heart and all thy counsel
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:4 requests that God grant according to the individual's heart and fulfill all their counsel, emphasizing personal petition and divine guidance.

questions.question: The word 'Selah' found in Psalms 20:3 is best understood as:
questions.correctAnswer: A musical pause or reflection
questions.explanation: Selah is a term used in Psalms indicating a pause or moment for contemplation, as found in Psalms 20:3.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the trust in God’s saving power expressed in Psalms 20:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 7:25
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7:25 speaks of Jesus saving those who come to God through Him, echoing the saving strength of God's right hand in Psalms 20:6.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:2 asks God to strengthen the petitioner from the sanctuary and from Zion.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:2 explicitly requests help from the sanctuary and strength from Zion, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 20:5 declares that the people will set up their banners in the name of foreign gods.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:5 states that banners will be set up in the name of our God, not foreign gods, making the statement false.

questions.question: What is the significance of 'the name of the God of Jacob' as mentioned in Psalms 20:1?
options: It represents the covenantal God of Israel
It refers to a pagan deity
It is a title for the king of Israel
It means the God of the Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the covenantal God of Israel
questions.explanation: In Psalms 20:1, 'the God of Jacob' signifies the covenantal God who defends Israel, emphasizing His faithfulness to His people.

questions.question: Which literary device is present in the contrast between those who trust in chariots and horses and those who remember the LORD in Psalms 20:7-8?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:7-8 uses antithesis by contrasting the trust in military power with trust in God, highlighting opposing outcomes.

questions.question: Which book in the Old Testament also frequently emphasizes the power of the LORD's right hand, connecting with Psalms 20:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus
questions.explanation: Exodus frequently refers to the power of the LORD's right hand, especially in the deliverance from Egypt, paralleling Psalms 20:6.

questions.question: In Psalms 20:5, what is the community's response to the king's salvation?
options: Rejoicing and setting up banners in God's name
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoicing and setting up banners in God's name
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:5 expresses communal joy in the king's salvation and the setting up of banners in the name of God as a sign of victory and trust.

questions.question: How does Psalms 20:6 indicate God’s attentiveness to His anointed one?
options: He will hear him from His holy heaven with saving strength
He will send a prophet to warn him
questions.correctAnswer: He will hear him from His holy heaven with saving strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:6 assures that God hears His anointed from heaven and delivers with strength, demonstrating divine attentiveness and power.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated in Psalms 20:1 where the LORD is asked to hear in the day of trouble?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine Protection
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:1 requests that the LORD hear in the day of trouble and defend by the name of the God of Jacob, highlighting His protective nature over His people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 20:2, from where does God send help and strength?
questions.correctAnswer: From the sanctuary and Zion
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:2 explicitly says God sends help from the sanctuary and strengthens from Zion, indicating the sacred place as the source of divine aid.

questions.question: What does Psalms 20:3 remind us God remembers and accepts?
options: All thy offerings and burnt sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: All thy offerings and burnt sacrifices
questions.explanation: Verse 3 focuses on God's remembrance and acceptance of offerings and burnt sacrifices, illustrating His responsiveness to worship practices.

questions.question: What does Psalms 20:4 promise God grants and fulfills?
options: According to thine own heart and counsel
questions.correctAnswer: According to thine own heart and counsel
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that God grants according to the heart and fulfills all counsel, emphasizing God's alignment with personal desires aligned with His will.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the communal rejoicing and trust expressed in Psalms 20:5?
options: Doctrine of Salvation and Covenant Community
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Salvation and Covenant Community
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows the community rejoicing in salvation and setting up banners in God's name, reflecting the doctrine of salvation and the covenant community’s shared faith.

questions.question: What essential Christological truth does Psalms 20:6 convey about the LORD and His anointed?
options: The LORD saves His anointed and hears from heaven
The LORD judges the nations through His anointed
The LORD forsakes His anointed in trials
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD saves His anointed and hears from heaven
questions.explanation: Psalms 20:6 reveals that the LORD saves His anointed and hears him from His holy heaven, foreshadowing the divine protection and intercession for the Messiah.

questions.question: What theological contrast is drawn in Psalms 20:7 between trusting chariots and horses versus remembering the name of the LORD?
options: Trust in military power versus trust in divine power
Trust in wealth versus trust in poverty
Trust in wisdom versus trust in folly
Trust in idols versus trust in prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in military power versus trust in divine power
questions.explanation: Verse 7 contrasts those who trust in chariots and horses (military might) with those who remember the name of the LORD, highlighting trust in divine rather than human strength.

questions.question: How does Psalms 20:8 describe the final outcome for those trusting in human strength compared to those trusting in God?
options: Those trusting in God are brought down
Those trusting in human strength fall, but God's people rise and stand upright
questions.correctAnswer: Those trusting in human strength fall, but God's people rise and stand upright
questions.explanation: Verse 8 describes those relying on chariots and horses as fallen, while God's people are risen and stand upright, affirming God's sustaining power.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 20 promotes militarism by trusting in chariots and horses. What does Psalms 20:7-8 actually teach about trust?
options: It advocates reliance on military power over God
It shows equal trust in God and military might
It rejects trust in military power and emphasizes trust in the LORD alone
It ignores the issue of trust
questions.correctAnswer: It rejects trust in military power and emphasizes trust in the LORD alone
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 clarify that some trust in chariots and horses but the faithful remember the LORD and stand upright, teaching exclusive trust in God rather than militarism.

questions.question: What does the plea in Psalms 20:9 reveal about the relationship between the king and the community?
options: The king rules without the people's call
The king is independent of God's help
The king depends on God's salvation and the people's united prayer
The king is only a military leader
questions.correctAnswer: The king depends on God's salvation and the people's united prayer
questions.explanation: Verse 9's plea for the LORD to save and let the king hear us when we call reveals the king's reliance on God's saving power and the community's intercession.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine assistance and human counsel is found by synthesizing Psalms 20:2 and Psalms 20:4?
options: God sends help from Zion and fulfills personal heart desires aligned with His counsel
God ignores human plans and only acts sovereignly
Help comes from human effort and God rarely intervenes
Divine help is only for the anointed king
questions.correctAnswer: God sends help from Zion and fulfills personal heart desires aligned with His counsel
questions.explanation: Verse 2 shows God sends help from the sanctuary, and verse 4 promises grant according to heart and counsel, teaching divine aid is both sovereign and responsive to godly plans.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about prayer and petition emerges from combining Psalms 20:5 and Psalms 20:9?
options: Petitions are unnecessary because God acts independently
Communal prayer and petitions are vital for salvation and the king's success
Only individual prayer matters, not communal
Petitions should be secret and silent
questions.correctAnswer: Communal prayer and petitions are vital for salvation and the king's success
questions.explanation: Verse 5 rejoices in salvation and petitions, while verse 9 calls for the king to hear communal calls, underscoring the importance of united prayer for divine intervention.

questions.question: How does the combination of Psalms 20:6 and Psalms 20:1 contribute to our understanding of God's saving power for His anointed?
options: God actively saves His anointed and hears from heaven in times of trouble
God ignores the prayers of the anointed
God saves only after human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God actively saves His anointed and hears from heaven in times of trouble
questions.explanation: Verse 1 petitions God to hear in trouble, and verse 6 confirms He saves His anointed and hears from heaven, teaching God's active involvement in salvation.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly seen in Psalms 20:6 regarding how He hears His anointed?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and attentive care
questions.explanation: Verse 6 references God hearing His anointed from His holy heaven, highlighting both His holiness and His personal, attentive care.

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative connection is suggested by the king's reliance on God's salvation in Psalms 20:9?
options: The king as a type of Christ who depends on God’s saving power
The king is rejected by God
The king is a symbol of earthly powers only
The king rules independently of God
questions.correctAnswer: The king as a type of Christ who depends on God’s saving power
questions.explanation: The king’s plea for salvation in verse 9 foreshadows Christ, the ultimate anointed king who fully depends on God’s saving power, fitting the messianic redemptive theme.
